claims.hypothesis: What causes the brightness asymmetry along the disk minor axis?
claims.experiment: Measured NE/SW flux ratio and compared with RADMC-3D synthetic images of Takakuwa et al.
claims.result: Flux ratio 1.17 (NE brighter), broadly consistent with models of a flared, optically thick dust disk
claims.finding: The asymmetry is probably caused by a flared dust distribution plus high optical depth, not necessarily substructure; other origins not ruled out

evidence.quote: probably caused by a flared distribution of the dust and the high optical depth of the dust emission

evidence.loc: 5.1 Brightness asymmetry, dust mass in the disk, and disk stability
evidence.quote: However, other reasons, such as non-axisymmetric internal structures, cannot be ruled out.

claims.hypothesis: What do the jets and outflows reveal about recent mass-ejection history?
claims.experiment: 12CO and SiO moment maps in velocity bins and PV diagrams along the jet axis
claims.result: Knotty, wiggling jets with a new inner knot pair (B0, R0); average ejection period ~73 yr; latest ejections ~20-25 yr ago
claims.finding: Episodic ejections occurred very recently, within the last ~25 years

evidence.quote: Our high angular resolution observations revealed the most recent mass ejection events, which have occurred within the last $\sim 25$ years.

referee_caveats_inferred: Mass range 0.15-0.39 Msun spans a factor of 2.6 and is set by method bias (ridge vs edge), not statistical error
Dust mass assumes optically thin emission while the asymmetry is attributed to high optical depth, an internal tension
Inclination of 47 deg comes from the Gaussian axis ratio under a thin-disk assumption yet is used for all kinematic and jet calculations
C18O edge p uncertainty differs between text (0.20) and Table 3 (0.22)
13CO and C18O PV diagrams show emission in all four quadrants (infall/outflow contamination) yet Keplerian fit uses restricted velocity ranges
Ring/gap significance rests on a residual after a two-Gaussian fit that is near the sensitivity limit, with width a fraction of the beam

Regions used for the NE/SW flux ratio and Toomre Q inputs (H/R)
Whether the archive holds the paper's final images is not stated
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Six EBs (4 C43-8, 2 C43-5) of a 1.3 mm continuum plus multi-line setup, likely several hundred GB of raw data; calibrated products would be far smaller
reproducibility.score_reason: Observations, software versions and key fit parameters are given and results are numeric, but most reduction details are deferred to the eDisk overview paper and self-calibration, imaging and fit settings are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: eDisk is an ALMA Large Program with a project code and the continuum Gaussian fit, dust mass and PV-fit stellar mass are numeric and redoable, though the two-pass self-calibration needs the eDisk scripts and the data archive status is not stated in the paper.
